name: Key West Run — January
subtitle: Savannah · Kennedy Space Center · Everglades · Key West · Naples · St Augustine · Charleston
summary: Fourteen days from Fort Lee to the bottom of the Florida Keys and back, driving the whole way. Two hard interstate days at each end buy you nine days of warm weather, the Everglades in dry season, and the Overseas Highway out to Key West. No flights, no big theme park, and four walkable historic cities on the same line.

mustSee.name: Forsyth Park
mustSee.why: Twenty-two squares, and this is the one at the end of them.

mustSee.name: Kennedy Space Center
mustSee.why: A flown shuttle and a complete Saturn V in one day.

mustSee.name: Anhinga Trail
mustSee.why: Alligators a few feet away, in the one month with no mosquitoes.

mustSee.name: Seven Mile Bridge
mustSee.why: The drive that makes the whole detour south worth it.

mustSee.name: Bahia Honda
mustSee.why: The best beach in the Keys, for $8 a vehicle.

mustSee.name: Mallory Square at sunset
mustSee.why: Every evening, free, and the reason to stay till dark.

mustSee.name: Southernmost Point
mustSee.why: The end of the road, 90 miles from Cuba.

mustSee.name: Naples Pier
mustSee.why: The Gulf side, flat and warm, after nine days of Atlantic.

mustSee.name: Castillo de San Marcos
mustSee.why: A Spanish fort from 1672, covered by the park pass.

mustSee.name: Rainbow Row
mustSee.why: Charleston on foot, which is the only way to do it.

watchOuts.title: Book Marathon and Kissimmee first
watchOuts.text: They are the two multi-night bases and the two that decide the budget. January is peak season in the Keys and the cheap Marathon rooms are the first to go. Everything else on this route can be booked late.

watchOuts.title: The Overseas Highway is the only road
watchOuts.text: US-1 runs 113 miles from Key Largo to Key West over 42 bridges, mostly one lane in each direction, with no alternative route at any point. An accident closes it. In January, in peak season, allow four hours from Homestead to Key West rather than the three the map promises.

watchOuts.title: Two days over 400 miles, and neither is optional
watchOuts.text: Day 2 is 467 miles and day 13 is 423, both on I-95. They are the price of reaching Key West from New Jersey in a fortnight. Day 2 is deliberately early, while everyone is still fresh.

watchOuts.title: Florida in January is peak season
watchOuts.text: The exact reverse of the desert. South Florida is at its most expensive precisely when the weather is best — Keys rooms above $275, Miami $250 to $450, Naples in full snowbird season. Central Florida is the cheap part, which is why three nights sit in Kissimmee.

watchOuts.title: Check the park pass is still in date
watchOuts.text: An America the Beautiful pass covers Everglades entry, Castillo de San Marcos and the Fort Sumter grounds — but it is an annual pass, so last year’s is no use. It does not cover the Fort Sumter ferry, Bahia Honda, or any Florida state park.

watchOuts.title: E-ZPass now works in Florida
watchOuts.text: It is accepted on all Florida toll roads, so there is no need for a separate SunPass. Do not carry two transponders in the vehicle at once — on the Central Florida expressways you can be billed on both accounts for the same trip.

watchOuts.title: Six people and fourteen days of luggage
watchOuts.text: A seven-seat minivan seats everyone but the space behind the third row is small. Either accept a roof box or take a full-size SUV, which costs more to hire and roughly $190 more in fuel over this distance. Price both before you book.

watchOuts.title: Confirm unlimited mileage before you book
watchOuts.text: This route covers about 3,350 miles. Anything charged per mile turns into a second rental fee — at $0.35 a mile that is close to $1,200. Major-brand car hire is normally unlimited; peer-to-peer motorhome listings usually are not.

watchOuts.title: New Jersey motorhomes are winterized until late March
watchOuts.text: Rigs in cold states are drained from about mid-October. You would pay to have it de-winterized to have running water, then start and finish the trip in freezing New Jersey with live plumbing. Burst pipes are charged to the renter.

watchOuts.title: The cheap Keys camping has already gone
watchOuts.text: Bahia Honda is $36 to $43 a night plus $7 for electric, and it books on an eleven-month window with Florida residents given first refusal and everyone else waiting another thirty days. For a January trip that window closes early the previous year. What is left is private Keys parks at $100 to $200 a night.

watchOuts.title: Key West turns away oversize vehicles
watchOuts.text: Most car parks in the old town will not take a 30-footer. Plan to leave it in Marathon, or check in advance which garages take oversize and what they charge.

pros: Key West and the Overseas Highway — 113 miles over 42 bridges, and not something you can do on a weekend from New Jersey.
The Everglades in dry season. January is the best month of the year to be there: the water is low so the wildlife concentrates, and the mosquitoes are gone.
No flights, no airport, no transfers for six people. The car is loaded at the front door.
Four walkable historic cities on the same line — Savannah, St Augustine, Charleston and Key West.
The theme park day costs about a third of Disney and is better pitched at children under twelve.
Warm from day 3 to day 11, and warmest at the far end where the schedule slows down.
cons: 3,350 miles, nearly 3,000 of it between towns. The Southwest Loop covers 1,655.
Two days over 400 miles, both on I-95, both unavoidable.
No mountains. January closes the Blue Ridge Parkway, Skyline Drive and Kuwohi Road, so the season takes away one of the four things this trip was meant to include.
Florida in January is peak season and the lodging prices show it — the exact reverse of the desert in winter.
The run home from Charleston is three days of interstate with very little on it.
One night each in Savannah and Charleston, which is not enough for either.

notConsidered.reason: Two days for six comes to $1,700–1,950 at January 2027 prices — more than the fuel, the tolls and every other ticket on this trip put together. LEGOLAND does the same job for the children for about $470.

Worse value than Disney for a two-day stop. Their two-day tickets include only a single Epic Universe day, and the version that actually works costs $484.57 an adult — around $2,900 for six. Full Epic access needs three days, which this itinerary has no room for.

notConsidered.place: Blue Ridge Parkway and the Smokies
notConsidered.reason: January closes them. Most of the Parkway sat shut through January 2026, Skyline Drive closes along its entire 105 miles for days at a time, and Kuwohi Road — the old Clingmans Dome Road — is gated from 1 December to 31 March. The mountains are the one draw this season cannot deliver.

notConsidered.place: A night in Key West itself
notConsidered.reason: Two rooms at $299–430 each. Marathon is 47 miles up the chain at a quarter of the price, and you still get the whole day and the sunset.
The ferry is around $200 a person, so $1,200 for six, and it consumes a full day out of Key West that this route does not have.
The route passes within thirty miles, but Miami rooms run $250–450 a night in January against a fraction of that in Homestead, and the city eats a day the schedule cannot spare.
Cold, windy and largely shut in January, and a long detour off I-95 for a beach nobody is going to swim at.
Wrong end of the calendar. Dark by half past four, most seasonal businesses closed, and the wrong direction entirely from a trip built around getting warm.

moneySavers.item: Sleep in Marathon, not Key West
moneySavers.detail: Key West rooms run $299–430 a night in January and six people need two of them. Marathon is 47 miles and 1h15 away. This is the largest single lever in the budget.
About $470 for six booked ahead against $1,700–1,950 for two Disney days. Children go from $39 on some January dates alongside a full-price adult.

moneySavers.item: Rent from a neighbourhood branch, not Newark Airport
moneySavers.detail: You are not flying, so there is no reason to pay the airport concession fee. A seven-seat van out of Jersey City runs about $68 a day in January against roughly $146 at Newark.
Thirty miles further from the beach, far closer to the Everglades gate, and less than half the price.

moneySavers.amount: $80, if yours is still in date
moneySavers.detail: Covers Everglades entry ($35 a vehicle), Castillo de San Marcos and the Fort Sumter grounds. It does not cover the Fort Sumter ferry, Bahia Honda or any state park.
Forty minutes further up the coast on day 10, out of the most expensive snowbird market in the state.
Gate price starts at $129 a head against roughly $90 adult and $67 child booked in advance.

options.name: Car and lodging
options.tagline: A hired van, thirteen nights booked
options.summary: The straightforward build, and the one this route is designed around. Hire a seven-seat van or a full-size SUV at home, book thirteen nights, and keep the vehicle small enough to park in four historic downtowns and drive into Key West. Costs more per night than camping and much less to fuel.

vehicle.detail: Chrysler Pacifica · Honda Odyssey · Toyota Sienna · Chevrolet Suburban
vehicle.notes: The van is cheaper to hire and much cheaper to fuel; the SUV is the one that swallows fourteen days of luggage for six without a roof box. Hire from a neighbourhood branch rather than Newark Airport — you are not flying, so there is no reason to pay the concession fee.

lines.basis: Seven-seat minivan against a full-size SUV, hired from a neighbourhood branch rather than Newark Airport. January is the cheapest month of the year for it.
3,350 miles at about 24 mpg in the van and 18 in the SUV, around $3.80 a gallon
Two rooms or one rental house. Three nights Kissimmee, two Homestead, two Marathon, the rest single nights.
Six people, fourteen days, eating out with breakfasts in
Six, booked online for a low-demand January date
Six, plus parking
Shark Valley tram for six, or an airboat at $26 to $40 a head
Only if day 13 starts late enough to allow it
The I-95 corridor and Florida’s Turnpike. E-ZPass is accepted throughout.
Key West garage, Bahia Honda $8 a vehicle, Blue Spring $6, Castillo covered by the park pass
Laundry, snacks, and the things that always come up

costs.notes: The gap between the columns is mostly vehicle and fuel — about $700 on the hire and $190 on fuel over 3,350 miles — with a little more headroom on lodging and food. If everyone travels light, the van is the better buy.

pros: Parks anywhere. Four of the best stops on this route are old towns with narrow streets.
Roughly $1,000 less in fuel than the motorhome over this distance.
Drives into Key West and parks there, which the motorhome largely cannot.
No de-winterizing, no plumbing to freeze on days 1, 2, 13 and 14.
cons: Lodging is the single biggest line in the budget, and January is peak season for half of it.
The two 400-mile days are spent belted into seats.

3.label: Worth knowing:
3.text: Kissimmee rental houses often come in under two hotel rooms and give you a kitchen for the three nights.

8.label: On the bridges:
8.text: The van handles the Overseas Highway like any other road. Watch the crosswind on the Seven Mile Bridge.

9.label: Drive right in:
9.text: Park once in an old-town garage and walk. Key West is about twelve blocks end to end.

options.name: Motorhome
options.tagline: Cheaper at the bottom, dearer at the top, awkward in the Keys
options.summary: A Class C hired in New Jersey. On paper it lands within a few hundred dollars of the car build — the campground and food savings very nearly cancel the hire and the fuel. What decides it is not the money: it is a winterized rig starting and finishing in a freezing New Jersey, no state park sites left in the Keys, and a 30-footer in Savannah, St Augustine, Charleston and Key West.

vehicle.detail: Sleeps 6 to 7 · 6 to 7 seatbelts · roughly 8 mpg
vehicle.notes: Book by seatbelt count rather than sleeping capacity. Confirm the mileage allowance in writing: at 3,350 miles, a 100-mile daily cap adds well over $500. Ask specifically whether the unit is winterized and what de-winterizing costs.

lines.basis: Class C hired in New Jersey. Peer-to-peer listings run $175 to $224 a night.
Peer-to-peer rentals typically include 100 to 150 miles a day. This route averages 239.
New Jersey rigs are drained from mid-October to late March
3,350 miles at 8 mpg. This single line is where the motorhome loses the argument.
Private Keys parks run $100 to $200 a night in January, and the state park sites are long gone.
Cooking in the motorhome with a few meals out
Bought at home rather than paying per-person kit fees
Six, booked online for a low-demand January date
Six, plus oversize parking
Shark Valley tram for six, or an airboat at $26 to $40 a head
Only if day 13 starts late enough to allow it
Higher than the car — most East Coast tolls are charged by axle and by height.
Key West garages that take an oversize vehicle are scarce and dear.
Propane, laundry, dump fees and showers

costs.notes: The low column assumes a flat-rate hire with unlimited mileage and state or county campgrounds wherever they can be got. The high column is a peer-to-peer hire with a daily mileage cap and private Keys parks at winter rates. The spread is wider than the car build because more of it is outside your control.

pros: The two 400-mile days are far more bearable when three children can get up and move.
No check-ins, and the food line drops by around $600.
Campgrounds outside the Keys are genuinely cheap in January.
cons: About $1,000 more in fuel at 8 mpg over 3,350 miles.
Winterized at both ends of the trip, with freeze damage charged to you.
The cheap Keys campsites were booked out a year ahead; what remains is dearer than the Marathon rooms.
Awkward or barred at four of the best stops on the route.

1.label: Winterized:
1.text: New Jersey rigs are drained from mid-October to late March. De-winterize it and you start and finish in freezing New Jersey with live plumbing.

2.label: This is the day it earns its keep:
2.text: 467 miles is a great deal more bearable when the children can get out of their seats.

7.label: Book early:
7.text: Long Pine Key and Flamingo both take motorhomes, but January is the busiest month in the Everglades.

8.label: Bahia Honda is gone:
8.text: The state park campground books on an eleven-month window with Florida residents first. For a January trip that closed early the previous year.

9.label: Not into Key West:
9.text: Most old-town car parks turn away oversize vehicles. Leave it in Marathon and take something smaller down, or check which garages take a 30-footer.

10.label: Take the Alley:
10.text: Alligator Alley is flat, straight and fine in a motorhome. The Tamiami Trail is narrower and much slower.

13.label: The other long one:
13.text: Same argument as day 2, over 423 miles.

days.headline: Down the Turnpike and out of the cold
days.notes: The one advantage of starting in Fort Lee is that you are already on the right side of the Hudson — no bridge toll, no Manhattan. Join the Turnpike, hold I-95 through Delaware and Maryland, and stop in Richmond. Nothing about this day is scenic. Leave early, because the stretch around Washington punishes anyone who arrives at four in the afternoon.
activities: Out by 7am to clear the Beltway before it seizes
Virginia State Capitol if you land with light to spare

days.headline: The long one
days.notes: The hardest day of the trip and there is no way to soften it — 467 miles of I-95 through the Carolinas. It is deliberately early, while everyone still has patience. South of Florence the pine gives way to marsh and the temperature finally starts to climb. You will reach Savannah after dark; the squares are worth a walk anyway.
activities: Break it at Santee or Walterboro
River Street after dark

pois.caption: Cobbled, right on the water, and lit up long after the drive is over.

photos.caption: Cobbled, right on the water, and lit up long after the drive is over.

days.headline: A morning in the squares, then south into the warm
days.notes: Savannah is laid out around 22 surviving squares and the way to see it is to walk four or five of them before the car starts again. Forsyth Park at the south end has the fountain everyone photographs. Then I-95 and the Florida line — the change is obvious somewhere past Jacksonville. Sleep in Kissimmee, which is where the cheap family rentals are.
activities: Walk Chippewa, Madison and Monterey squares
Forsyth Park fountain
Into Kissimmee by evening — three nights here

pois.name: Forsyth Park
pois.caption: The fountain at the south end of the squares, under live oaks and Spanish moss.

photos.caption: The fountain at the south end of the squares, under live oaks and Spanish moss.

days.headline: The theme park day, at a third of the price
days.notes: LEGOLAND Florida is 34 miles down the road at Winter Haven, built on the old Cypress Gardens site — the botanical gardens are still standing behind the rides. January is their lowest-demand pricing and the park is pitched squarely at children up to about twelve. Adults from roughly $90 and children from $67 booked ahead, with dates where a child goes for $39 alongside a full-price adult.
activities: Book online — the gate price is close to double
The original Cypress Gardens botanical gardens are inside the park
Bok Tower Gardens is 20 minutes away for a quieter afternoon

photos.caption: Built on the old Cypress Gardens site — the botanical gardens are still behind the rides.

days.headline: Rockets
days.notes: Fifty-six miles east to the Space Coast, and a full day once you are there. Space Shuttle Atlantis hangs at an angle a few feet from the glass with its payload doors open, and the bus out to the Apollo/Saturn V Center puts you underneath a complete Saturn V lying on its side. Adult admission runs about $88 at the gate and less on promotion. Parking is charged separately.
activities: Atlantis first, before the queues build
Take the bus tour early — the last one leaves mid-afternoon
Check whether anything is launching on your dates

pois.name: Kennedy Space Center
pois.caption: Space Shuttle Atlantis hangs a few feet from the glass with its payload doors open.

photos.caption: Space Shuttle Atlantis hangs a few feet from the glass with its payload doors open.

pois.name: Vehicle Assembly Building
pois.caption: One of the largest buildings in the world by volume. The bus tour runs past it.

days.headline: Down the spine of Florida
days.notes: The Turnpike most of the way, then the agricultural land south of Miami. Homestead is not a destination — it is where you sleep to be at the Everglades gate in the morning, and it costs a fraction of anywhere closer to the city.
activities: Stock up in Homestead — there is nothing in the park
Two nights here

days.headline: Dry season, which is the whole point
days.notes: January is the best month of the year to be here. The water is low so the wildlife concentrates in what is left of it, and the mosquitoes that make summer unbearable have gone. Two ends worth seeing: the Anhinga Trail at Royal Palm, where alligators lie on the bank a few feet from a boardwalk, and Shark Valley off the Tamiami Trail, where a two-hour tram runs a fifteen-mile loop out to an observation tower.
activities: Anhinga Trail early — an easy half-mile boardwalk
Shark Valley tram, or rent bikes and ride the loop yourselves
$35 a vehicle for seven days, or nothing at all on the America the Beautiful pass

days.headline: Onto the Overseas Highway
days.notes: Eighty miles, but do not treat it as a short day — this is the drive. US-1 leaves the mainland at Key Largo and runs 113 miles over 42 bridges, mostly two lanes with water on both sides. The Seven Mile Bridge is the one from the photographs, with the abandoned 1912 railway bridge running alongside it. Stop at Bahia Honda on the way in; it has the best beach in the Keys.
activities: Seven Mile Bridge
Bahia Honda State Park, $8 a vehicle
Check in at Marathon, roughly halfway down the chain

days.headline: Key West for the day, Marathon for the night
days.notes: Forty-seven miles down and the same back. Sleeping in Marathon rather than Key West is the single biggest saving on this trip — Key West rooms run $299 to $430 in January and six people need two of them. Park once and walk, because the old town is small. Mallory Square holds a sunset gathering every evening with buskers and it costs nothing.
activities: Park in a garage and leave the car there
Southernmost Point marker — expect a queue
Hemingway House if the six-toed cats appeal
Mallory Square for sunset, then the drive back

days.headline: Back up the Keys and across the bottom of the state
days.notes: Retrace the Overseas Highway, then cut west on Alligator Alley or the slower Tamiami Trail. Naples is the warmest night of the trip and the most expensive — peak snowbird season and the town knows it. Fort Myers is forty minutes further on and materially cheaper if the number bothers you.
activities: Naples Pier at sunset
White sand and a flat Gulf, after nine days of Atlantic

pois.name: Naples Pier
pois.caption: Thousand feet of boardwalk into a flat Gulf, and the warmest evening of the trip.

photos.caption: Thousand feet of boardwalk into a flat Gulf, and the warmest evening of the trip.

days.headline: North to the oldest city
days.notes: Up I-75 and across the state. St Augustine was founded in 1565, which makes it the oldest continuously occupied European settlement in the country, and it wears it well — the old town is genuinely old rather than reconstructed.
activities: Walk St George Street in the evening
The fort opens at nine tomorrow — do it before you drive

pois.name: St Augustine Old Town

photos.caption: Deep verandas and palms in a town founded in 1565 — genuinely old, not reconstructed.

days.headline: A fort in the morning, Charleston by evening
days.notes: Castillo de San Marcos opens at nine — a Spanish coquina fort on the harbour, begun in 1672 and never taken by force. The America the Beautiful pass covers it. Then north into South Carolina, where Charleston's peninsula is one long walk: Rainbow Row, the Battery, and the houses behind them.
activities: Castillo de San Marcos first thing
Rainbow Row and the Battery on foot
Book dinner — Charleston fills up even in January

days.headline: The second long one
days.notes: The last hard day. If you want Fort Sumter you need the first boat out and a much later start, which turns 423 miles into an evening arrival — decide the night before rather than at breakfast. Otherwise walk the Battery at first light and get moving.
activities: Fort Sumter is 2h15 round trip by ferry — only if you are willing to leave after lunch
Break at Fayetteville or Rocky Mount

days.headline: Home
days.notes: The reverse of day one, and the reason day 13 stopped at Richmond instead of pushing further north. Aim to clear Washington and Baltimore before the afternoon builds. Coming back into Fort Lee from the south there is no bridge toll.
activities: Through Washington before 2pm or pay for it in time
